title: MediEvil 2
subtitle: Sir Daniel wakes in the wrong century
summary: MediEvil 2 is Sony Cambridge's PlayStation action-adventure, first released in Europe on 21 April 2000. Sir Daniel Fortesque returns five hundred years after his earlier adventure, finding himself in Victorian London while Lord Palethorn's plans bring the dead back into the city. The change of period gives the familiar skeletal hero another kind of Gothic setting to stumble through. Weapons, exploration and eccentric encounters continue the original's mixture of horror and comedy. Daniel remains an unlikely champion, whose alarming appearance rarely matches the dignity with which he would like to be remembered.
body: MediEvil 2 is Sony Cambridge's PlayStation action-adventure, first released in Europe on 21 April 2000. Sir Daniel Fortesque returns five hundred years after his earlier adventure, finding himself in Victorian London while Lord Palethorn's plans bring the dead back into the city. The change of period gives the familiar skeletal hero another kind of Gothic setting to stumble through. Weapons, exploration and eccentric encounters continue the original's mixture of horror and comedy. Daniel remains an unlikely champion, whose alarming appearance rarely matches the dignity with which he would like to be remembered.

Dan can keep two weapons ready and switch between them during a fight. Pistols, blunderbusses and a gatling gun join his older swords and shields, while defeating enemies fills a Chalice of Souls that can earn further equipment. Later, placing his detached head on a zombified hand creates Dan Hand. The player can alternate between the crawling head and the body, exploring openings that the full skeleton cannot enter. The grotesque joke becomes a way to investigate the environment, giving an apparently familiar hero another useful shape.

Sony commissioned the Cambridge team to continue MediEvil after the first game's favourable reception. Several concepts were considered before the Victorian Gothic revival became the chosen setting. James Shepherd directed, with Andrew Barnabas and Paul Arnold returning to compose the score. North America received the sequel in May 2000. Reviews generally welcomed the refinements while noting its close relationship to the original. MediEvil 2 keeps the series' personality intact by changing the place and period around Daniel, allowing a familiar comic figure to encounter another collection of wonderfully inappropriate dangers.
story_headings: Sir Daniel wakes in the wrong century
A familiar hero in unfamiliar streets
A sequel made before the PlayStation moved on
